scandals.casa_blanca: Casa Blanca — Conflict of interest: presidential family linked to contractor Grupo Higa (EPN, 2014)
scandals.estafa_maestra: La Estafa Maestra — MXN 7.6B diverted through public universities using ghost companies (EPN, 2017)
scandals.odebrecht: Odebrecht-PEMEX — Brazilian engineering firm paid bribes for infrastructure contracts (Calderón/EPN, 2010–2016)
scandals.pemexgate: PEMEXGATE — PEMEX funds routed through the oil workers' union to the PRI's 2000 presidential campaign; the IFE fined the PRI in 2003 (Fox term)
scandals.segalmex: Segalmex — the SFP reports MXN 2.7B diverted; the ASF observed MXN 8.6B in the 2020 accounts (audit observations, not final determinations) (AMLO, 2021)
scandals.tren_maya: Tren Maya — FONATUR awarded MXN 180M in direct contracts to Army without civilian bidding (AMLO, 2023)
scandals.efos_sat: SAT EFOS Definitivo — 38 COMPRANET vendors confirmed as ghost companies by Mexico's tax authority (AMLO, 2022)
scandals.grupo_higa: Grupo Higa / Casa Blanca — infrastructure contractor with direct presidential family conflict of interest (EPN, 2014)

contexts.fox: Vicente Fox's 2000 victory broke 71 years of PRI rule. As the first PAN president, his administration prioritized economic transparency and launched COMPRANET as a digital procurement platform — but inherited deeply entrenched patronage networks.
contexts.calderon: Felipe Calderón won a disputed 2006 election by a margin of 0.56%. His administration launched a militarized 'war on drugs' that reshaped federal spending, driving large emergency-exempt contracts in defense and security sectors.
contexts.pena_nieto: Enrique Peña Nieto's PRI returned to power in 2012 promising modernization. His six years saw some of Mexico's most high-profile corruption investigations — Casa Blanca, La Estafa Maestra, and Odebrecht-PEMEX — which exposed significant gaps in procurement oversight.
contexts.amlo: Andrés Manuel López Obrador won the 2018 election by the largest margin in modern Mexican history (53%). His self-described 'Fourth Transformation' centralized procurement power, reaching a record 78.9% direct award rate while bypassing competitive bidding, citing austerity and anti-corruption goals.
contexts.sheinbaum: Claudia Sheinbaum, elected June 2024 with 59% of the vote, is Mexico's first female president. A climate scientist by training, she took office October 1, 2024, inheriting AMLO's institutional structures. Her first months show a directional decline in direct awards, though continuity risks remain high.
